phases.name: Customers and Products
known_risks: Public APIs, product images, and external references remain deferred.

phases.name: Orders
known_risks: Confirmed-order snapshots intentionally retain the approved minimum personal data and require masking discipline.

phases.name: Fulfillment
known_risks: Concurrent partial allocations must never exceed the confirmed OrderItem quantity.
Delivery snapshots contain personal data and require the same masking and sanitization discipline as Orders.
Order cancellation and fulfillment execution are separate lifecycles and require an explicit, idempotent coordination rule.

phases.name: Payments
known_risks: A provider callback may contain PII and card metadata that must never be persisted raw or copied to logs, AuditEvent, OutboxEvent, or command receipts.
Multiple active hosted checkout links can create duplicate or excess payment; the canonical domain must serialize attempts and surface inconsistencies for manual reconciliation.
Pagar.me webhook authenticity requirements are not explicit in the public v5 documentation reviewed and must be confirmed before enabling its callback in any environment.
Order cancellation after a successful payment requires an explicit no-refund handling rule because refunds and chargebacks are deferred.

phases.name: Messaging
known_risks: A provider may accept a message while the client observes a timeout; blind retry can duplicate a customer communication.
A checkout link can expire, be cancelled, or be replaced between message creation and dispatch and therefore requires exact source revalidation immediately before send.
Contact existence is not permission to message; missing, stale, or suppressed per-purpose evidence must fail closed and the Organization remains responsible for its LGPD legal basis.
Delivery callbacks can contain recipient data, arrive duplicated or out of order, and must be authenticated, minimized, and mapped monotonically.
Automatic event-driven communication can amplify configuration errors, so every Organization rule starts disabled and remains limited to an explicit event/template allowlist.

Evolution API linked-device is a non-official WhatsApp connection, has no documented send idempotency key or payload-bound webhook signature in the adopted stable contract, and requires explicit operational risk acceptance, version pinning, isolated infrastructure, and no blind retry.
Evolution API 2.4 is currently presented as a pre-release with a licensing activation change; no upgrade or production adoption may occur without a new license, security, and compatibility review.

phases.name: Integrations
known_risks: Reference adapter validates architecture offline but does not constitute homologation of any concrete external provider.

Integrations task module has low direct line coverage because behavior is exercised primarily through services and runtime topology; critical service paths and registration are covered by direct tests/CI.
Inbound WhatsApp sales conversations remain outside this generic Integrations tranche and require explicit future domain scope.

phases.name: Dashboard and complete experience
known_risks: Dashboard remains a synchronous derived read model and may require projection/cache work at higher volume.
Future dashboard relations must preserve explicit tenant scoping on both root objects and every traversed relation.
Attention queues must remain derived from canonical domain states and must not become an independent lifecycle.

phases.name: Infrastructure and homologation
known_risks: Homologation depends on a PostgreSQL 17 resource that is external to the application Compose stack and must remain private and exclusive.
Backup configuration is not sufficient evidence until a restore into an empty temporary database is actually demonstrated.
Provider and callback homologation remains separately gated and must not be inferred from the base infrastructure deployment.
